newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria plans tax to tackle decaying capital.
newsitem.headline: Algeria plans tax to tackle decaying capital.

text.p: Algeria is planning to levy an accommodation tax to finance work on the capital's housing, which has reached a state of advanced decay, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Wednesday.
The tax, expected to raise 400 million dinars ($7.27 million) a year, will go to finance a 10-year programme to tackle Algiers' crumbling buildings.

Algiers, the capital city, was built to house around 750,000 people but now has a population estimated at between three and four million, with many extended families of up to 12 people living in tiny apartments.

Overall cost of the refurbishment project is set at 10 billion dinars, APS said, adding that the project was included in the finance law for 1997 being discussed on Wednesday by the National Transitional Council.
